answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation expensive to fake: require each agent to build a long, verifiable thread of completed work before it can earn trust or rewards. A lone comet that streaks in, does one flashy job, and vanishes should stay untrusted, while a falcon that returns again and again, with its history checkable on the ledger, earns standing. Sybils can copy an identity, but they cannot cheaply copy months of attested work.
